title: How a tap stays smooth
subtitle: update() and view() decide on the UI thread; slow work runs on job threads and comes back as an event

nodes.label: Screen
nodes.desc: Every platform draws on one thread. At 60 Hz it has about 16 ms per frame.

nodes.label: UI thread
nodes.desc: Only decides: changes state and describes the screen. The app's state is only touched here, so no locks and no races in app code.

nodes.label: Watchdog
nodes.desc: Names any update(), view() or draw over the budget (SLOW: update msg=7 80 ms), on every host, before a user sees the freeze.

nodes.label: Query job
nodes.desc: A query, an import or a sort on its own thread. It owns a snapshot of its inputs.

nodes.label: Video decoder
nodes.desc: A decoder thread per video: opens in about 40 µs, seeks in about 6 µs, the newest seek wins.

nodes.label: Document job
nodes.desc: Reading a folder of PDFs, drawing pages and writing claim packs, off the UI thread.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.desc: The heavy lifting: group-bys, medians, image ops.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.desc: Tables in memory and on the GPU.

zones.label: job threads: do the slow part

flows.name: A slow query, a live window
flows.desc: A tap asks for a median over 100M rows.

steps.note: The tap reaches update() as an event.
update() starts a job with a snapshot of what it needs, and returns at once.
The window keeps drawing: the island shows progress every frame.
The job runs the median on the GPU.
The job ends and wakes the main loop; update() hears it as an ordinary event.
view() draws the answer. Measured: a 1.5 s job, 90 frames while it ran, the longest gap 17 ms.
Each drag step is an event.
update() asks the decoder thread to seek; it never waits for the frame.
Only the newest seek is decoded; older ones are dropped.
The frame lands and wakes the UI.
The new frame is drawn in the next frame.
